title: Spin-Locking on Uniprocessor
pattern: Using a pure spinlock on a system with only a single CPU core (uniprocessor).
why_bad: A thread spinning in a tight loop on a uniprocessor consumes 100% of the single CPU's resources. Because the thread holding the lock cannot get a scheduling quantum to execute and release the lock, the spinning thread wastes its entire scheduling slice, severely degrading performance.
detection: Spinlocks used in a deployment target or system environment compiled for or limited to a single CPU core without yields.
counterexample: The spinlock contains an explicit thread yield or sleep command, which immediately returns scheduling control to the OS.
